name: Agreement between the Delaware and Wyandot, 1843
aka: Delaware sale of 39 sections to the Wyandot at the mouth of the Kansas River
promises: This is an agreement between two nations, not with the United States. Article 1: the Delaware gave the Wyandot three sections at the junction of the Missouri and Kansas rivers.
Article 2: the Delaware sold the Wyandot thirty-six further sections adjoining them.
Article 3: the Wyandot would pay the Delaware $46,080 over eleven years.
Congress ratified it in 1848 with the proviso that the Wyandot would take no better right in the land than the Delaware held.
today: No land passed to the United States under this agreement. The 1850 Wyandot treaty (kappler-595) states that the Wyandot had to buy this land because the United States never gave them the 148,000 acres promised in 1842.

openQuestions: Royce lists area 263 under this agreement, but it is a sale between nations, not a cession to the United States. The map may be showing a Delaware-to-Wyandot sale as a US taking.
The breach behind this agreement belongs to the Wyandot treaty of March 17, 1842, whose findings file should carry the 1850 admission.

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for Delaware and Wyandot (Court of Claims index) and 'Delaware Wyandot 1843', 'Wyandot December 14 1843' (ICC); only Pawnee and Potawatomi decisions that mention the date; nothing on this agreement.

plain.promised: The Delaware gave and sold 39 sections near the Kansas-Missouri river junction to the Wyandot for $46,080. The United States was not a party; Congress approved it in 1848.
plain.happened: No finding of a broken promise concerns this agreement itself.
plain.today: The Wyandot needed this land because the United States never gave them the western land promised in 1842.
